question: Which nerve is most at risk in a posterior dislocation of the hip?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The femoral nerve is at risk in anterior hip dislocation, not posterior. It runs anterior to the hip joint in close proximity to the femoral head in its anterior position.

Correct. In posterior hip dislocation, the femoral head is driven posteriorly and can stretch or compress the sciatic nerve (specifically its peroneal division), which passes posterior to the hip. Foot drop is the most common neurological complication. Always test sciatic nerve function before and after reduction.
The obturator nerve is at risk with medial wall acetabular fractures, not classic posterior hip dislocation. It passes through the obturator foramen medially.
The lateral femoral cutaneous nerve is at risk from surgical approaches (especially anterior) or meralgia paraesthetica, not from posterior hip dislocation. It is a purely sensory nerve.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review nerve-joint pairings: posterior hip dislocation = sciatic nerve; anterior shoulder dislocation = axillary nerve; posterior knee dislocation = popliteal artery + common peroneal nerve; elbow dislocation = median/radial nerve.

Correct. Posterior hip dislocation → sciatic nerve (peroneal division). The mnemonic: posterior HIP = sciatic. Anterior hip = femoral nerve. Anterior shoulder = axillary nerve (test deltoid power and regimental badge sensation).
